description:
Advances: ancora.derive

Wave 2 of ancora-gg8, sequenced AFTER ancora-xla.3 merges (to avoid gate.ex/compare.ex churn against xla.3's materialize/hoist/parse-once fixes). D items 4-5 in the investigation record; findings-DE and the architecture decision are comments on the epic. The dominant measured cost is repeated sequential parsing: ~9s of single-threaded Code.string_to_quoted work at atlas scale (818 lib files parsed 2-3x per side, 695 test files, 216 spec files). The review dropped parallelization as F68 on a Livebook-scale 330ms measurement with an explicit revisit-if-latency-reported clause — that clause has triggered.

Deliverable:
1. Parallelize the four sequential parse loops with Task.async_stream (the pattern Derive.run already sets, lib/ancora/derive.ex:63-68): ModuleLocator.scan_sources (lib/ancora/derive/module_locator.ex:97-107), TagScanner.scan (lib/ancora/tag_scanner.ex:52-73), the def_indexes build (lib/ancora/gate.ex:291-303), and Index.build's subject parse loop. Determinism holds by construction: collect results in input order, and when multiple files fail to parse, the first error by path order wins — pin both properties with tests.
2. One parse per (side, file) across the ModuleLocator -> DefIndex leg: ModuleLocator currently parses every lib file and discards the ASTs; DefIndex re-reads and re-parses the same files. Extend xla.3's parse-once threading shape from Compare to this leg (~1.4s per side). Respect the run-scoped memo contract: parsed products live in the per-run ETS table passed by reference (ancora.derive.memo_is_run_scoped), never named, never on disk.

Spec delta: none required — behavior is contract-identical (finding order, membership, and output must not change). If review of the memo contract's wording suggests recording the parse-once guarantee, that is a statement edit to ancora.derive.memo_is_run_scoped in this diff; otherwise leave specs untouched.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: full existing suite; determinism property tests — same corpus parsed N times yields identical finding lists including order; a fixture with two unparseable files always reports the path-order-first error; the two-concurrent-runs scenario still passes (no cross-run memo bleed).
- Behaviors to demonstrate: timing before/after on the ancora corpus and, if reachable, the atlas corpus via --root; post-merge, run the median-of-3 warm bench that feeds the ancora-u38 revisit decision and record numbers in the IMPLEMENTED comment.
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale plus targeted files, and mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: before IMPLEMENTED, full mix test plus mix spec.check --base <stage-base>, run-until-green.
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base <stage-base> and targeted/--stale selections only; no full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path
  - Fixture/sandbox hygiene: async-safe fixtures, no cross-test leakage
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable/config surface
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test
- Call-site Integration: no new callable surface; all four loops are on existing gate/report paths, proven by the golden subprocess tests.

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/ancora/output*.ex
- lib/ancora/finding.ex
- lib/ancora/severity.ex
- lib/ancora/config.ex
- lib/ancora/prime.ex, lib/ancora/next.ex, lib/ancora/status.ex (the waste fixes landed in wave 1)

Allowed touches (this stage may modify):
- lib/ancora/derive/module_locator.ex
- lib/ancora/derive/def_index.ex
- lib/ancora/tag_scanner.ex
- lib/ancora/index.ex
- lib/ancora/gate.ex (def_indexes wiring only)
- lib/ancora/derive/run_context.ex (memo threading)
- test/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md (only the optional memo_is_run_scoped wording noted above, plus acknowledgment edits for this stage's own changes only)

Out of Scope (intent):
- No caching across runs, in memory or on disk (ancora-u38 stays deferred by ruling; its revisit bench runs after this ticket)
- No unbounded concurrency — Task.async_stream with default max_concurrency and back-pressure
- No changes to resolver purity (ancora.derive.resolver_is_pure) or the batch-port serial prefetch contract (ancora.derive.base_reads_batched)
- No output changes of any kind

Merge gate:
- [ ] Code compiles cleanly
- [ ] Tests listed above pass
- [ ] Spec verification passes
- [ ] Scope check: diff touches only Allowed globs (mechanical)
- [ ] Auditor APPROVE comment on the ticket

ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: still blocked, now on the ancora-xla epic rather than xla.3 alone

ancora-xla.3 closed at 00:52Z, merged into ancora-xla/post-ship-hardening (that epic's branch), not into main. This ticket's second deliverable extends xla.3's parse-once threading shape and touches gate.ex and compare.ex, so its base must contain xla.3's code. The ancora-gg8 epic branch does not, and mixing another epic's branch into this one is not the orchestrator's call. Dependency re-pinned: ancora-xla blocks ancora-gg8.7. Runnable once ancora-xla has merged to main and ancora-gg8/field-friction has been rebased onto it (or once Manuel rules otherwise). The gg8 orchestration run will finish without this ticket and report it as set aside.

DECISION (Manuel, 2026-09-04): this ticket runs in the field-friction epic after all, once ancora-xla merges to main. Sequence: ancora-xla PR merges; ancora-gg8/field-friction is rebased onto origin/main (a rebase worker, per protocol); this ticket is admitted with the rebased tip as its base. Its Allowed touches and Advances must be re-checked against that tip at admission, since xla.3 and gg8.4/gg8.5 all touched gate.ex and the parsing path.

ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT AMENDMENT at admission (2026-09-04, base e6d5443 = epic tip containing release 1.1.0). Main's accepted decision ancora.decision.no_run_context_memo removed RunContext's ETS table and its memo functions ("Parse reuse remains plain data passed to comparison code"; "any new repeated work must first justify machinery beyond plain function arguments"). So deliverable 2 is re-read as follows, nothing else in the ticket changes:

- Deliverable 2 (parse once per (side, file) across ModuleLocator -> DefIndex): thread the parsed ASTs as plain data. ModuleLocator keeps the AST (or the parsed source product) it already produces per file and returns it alongside the module map; Gate.def_indexes/2 consumes those products instead of re-reading and re-parsing the files. This extends the parse-once shape 1.1.0 already uses between the gate and Compare. No ETS, no named process, no cache across runs; ancora.derive.memo_is_run_scoped stays true by construction and needs no wording change unless the statement text mentions the removed table (then edit that sentence in this diff).
- Allowed touches: lib/ancora/derive/run_context.ex is dropped (nothing to thread there). lib/ancora/gate.ex is allowed for the ModuleLocator -> def_indexes handoff and the def_indexes parallelization, still nothing else in that file. The rest of the list stands: module_locator.ex, def_index.ex, tag_scanner.ex, index.ex, test/**, .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md (acknowledgment edits for this stage's own changes only).
- Deliverable 1 stands unchanged: the four loops are still sequential on e6d5443 (module_locator.ex reduce_while over sources, tag_scanner.ex reduce over test files, gate.ex def_indexes/2, index.ex Enum.map over spec files).
- Out of scope, restated: no changes to lib/ancora/derive/compare.ex or the ChangeSet/batch-port path that 1.1.0 rewrote; if parse-once needs a Compare signature change, post SCOPE_EXPANSION.
- Benchmark clause: record before/after timings on the ancora corpus in the IMPLEMENTED record; the atlas corpus via --root only if reachable.

Under that same mutation Gate.check(".", base: "HEAD") on the ancora repo itself returns 10 findings in a different order on each of three runs, and Index.build subject order differs run to run. That is exactly the contract violation the ticket says to pin ("same corpus parsed N times yields identical finding lists including order"), and nothing catches it.
- Mutation on lib/ancora/gate.ex:426 (def_indexes ordered: false plus jitter) also survives, but that one is benign: the result is a map keyed by module, so collection order cannot reach output, and DefIndex.build/2 on an AST cannot fail, leaving only the Map.fetch miss on the error branch.
- Fix: give the determinism fixture several spec files with ordering-sensitive findings (unresolved anchors or drift across two or more subjects) and several lib files, then keep the existing full-list equality across runs. N=5 is thin for a race; 10 or more costs little on this fixture.

Restoring the e6d5443 def_indexes body (File.read plus DefIndex.build(source, path)) fails it at gate_test.exs:757 with the intended message. trace_pattern is cleared and the forwarder stopped in on_exit; the module is async: false (gate_test.exs:5).

Output.sort_findings sorts by severity only and is stable, so subject order leaks straight into the report. The determinism test at test/ancora/gate_test.exs:761 cannot see this because its fixture has only two test files and no spec files beyond the .keep, so subject count is 0 to 1 there. This confirms the TEST_CRITIC finding. A fixture with several spec files, asserting subject order in the index or finding order across runs, would close it; the failing seed is not needed since the reorder shows up on every run at 8 files.

Notes:

Not a Gap.
- Behavior shift on repos with two or more unparseable lib files: at e6d5443 ModuleLocator iterated a map of sources, so for more than 32 files the first-reported error followed map hash order. 02a00f1 sorts by path first. That is what the ticket asked for and output is identical on this repo, but a consumer with multiple broken lib files may see a different (now path-first) file named in derived/unparseable_source than before.
- TagScanner and Index now exit the caller on a task crash ({:exit, reason} -> exit(reason)) where the old sequential code would have raised in place. Same failure class (run aborts), different exception shape; only matters for a crash inside scan_file or Parser.parse_file.

AUDIT: BOUNCE → implementer
Session: e92f6de6-94f7-4814-8140-19f3f3007d0a

Reasoning: Both graders' Gap is real and I reproduced it in a scratch copy of 02a00f1 (stage untouched). With lib/ancora/index.ex:85 set to ordered: false plus jitter, the six targeted files pass (119 tests, 0 failures), while on this repo Index.build returned 8 distinct subject orders in 8 runs, Gate.check(root, base: "e6d5443") returned 17 findings in 4 distinct orders across 8 runs (same set), and two of three rendered `mix spec.check --base e6d5443 --verbose` outputs differed in finding order. The determinism test at test/ancora/gate_test.exs:762 cannot see this because create_clean_repo (gate_test.exs:1383) writes only mix.exs and .spec/specs/.keep, so the Index.build, ModuleLocator and def_indexes loops run over empty input there. The other three loops are pinned as reported: tag_scanner.ex ordered: false fails gate_test.exs:762 at line 783; module_locator.ex ordered: false fails module_locator_test.exs:77 (lib/z_fast_error.ex reported); gate.ex def_indexes ordered: false survives but is an equivalent mutant (results fold into a map keyed by module, Map.fetch cannot miss, DefIndex.build/2 on an AST cannot fail; 1 finding order in 8 real-repo runs). Scope and trailer checks in the VERIFY comment match the diff: 8 files, gate.ex hunk limited to the two def_indexes call lines and the def_indexes/2 body, test/** additions only, one Spec-Ack trailer, compare.ex and run_context.ex untouched. Deliverable 1 says "pin both properties with tests"; the order property is unpinned for one of the four loops, so this is a coverage bounce, not a mechanical remedy.

Bounce reason: test-only fix. No production code and no spec text needs to change. Required changes, all in test/ancora/gate_test.exs:

1. Rework the fixture of "parallel parsing preserves complete finding order across runs" (gate_test.exs:762) so every parallelized loop has real input. Keep the git init and commit. Write: mix.exs; at least four spec files under .spec/specs/ covering at least two distinct subjects; at least three lib files each defining its own module (so ModuleLocator.scan_sources and Gate.def_indexes run over several paths); and keep the two unparseable test files (the padded test/a_slow_error_test.exs and test/z_fast_error_test.exs) so the TagScanner pin stays.

2. Make the spec findings order-sensitive at the same severity so subject order is the only thing that decides their position after Output.sort_findings (lib/ancora/output.ex:149 sorts by rank only and is stable). For example, give each subject a requirement anchored to a tag no test carries, so each subject yields at least one finding, or use any finding code that is emitted once per subject. Make the path-first spec file heavy (a long body, the same trick as the 20k-line test file) so that under plain `ordered: false` with no jitter its completion lands late and the reorder actually shows.

3. Run the real production path, Gate.check(root, base: "HEAD"), not Index.build directly, N >= 10 times. Assert full-list equality of report.all_findings across all runs, including order (the existing Enum.all? against hd is fine). Also add a fixed-expectation assertion: the subject-attributable findings, mapped to {subject, code} or {file, code}, equal the path-sorted expected list. Without that second assertion the test passes whenever all N runs happen to agree. Keep the existing tags/parse_error file-order assertion.

4. Proof in the new IMPLEMENTED record, done in a scratch copy: (a) lib/ancora/index.ex:85 `ordered: false`, with and without jitter, fails the named test at its assertion line; (b) lib/ancora/tag_scanner.ex ordered: false still fails the same test; (c) lib/ancora/derive/module_locator.ex ordered: false still fails module_locator_test.exs:77; (d) the unmutated six targeted files (module_locator_test, def_index_test, gate_test, tag_scanner_test, index_test, spec_check_test) are green.
